subject: physics
question_text: Check the correctness of the equation v² = u² + 2as using dimensional analysis.

verification.note: PREDICTED CELL — not asked by either source book. Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in the Fastrack (pp.4-5) or the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3), so it is authored as a 2-mark VSAQ like every other Unit 2 card. Both the question and the 1+1 mark split are CLAIMS until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Dimensions of each term
lines: The 2 is a pure number and has no dimensions.
steps.why: The constant 2 is dropped because a pure number has dimensions M⁰L⁰T⁰, so it cannot change the dimensional formula of the term it multiplies.
common_mistakes: Giving the 2 a dimension of its own.
Squaring only the L in v² and leaving T⁻¹ unsquared.

recall.must_convey: That all three terms have dimensions L squared T to the minus two.

steps.memory_tip: Square the WHOLE bracket: [L T⁻¹]² = L² T⁻², not L² T⁻¹.
steps.margin_note: One line per term keeps the comparison visible.

steps.label: The verdict

lines.text: All three terms have the same dimensions

steps.why: Dimensional correctness is necessary but not sufficient, so the honest verdict is "dimensionally correct" rather than simply "correct".
common_mistakes: Writing only "correct". The check establishes dimensional correctness alone.

recall.must_convey: That the equation is dimensionally correct because all terms match.

steps.memory_tip: Write "dimensionally correct" — the word dimensionally is the honest part.

insider_note: Take each term separately and show all three match. Ending with a verdict sentence is what closes the answer.
